Maladaptive Strategies.value: wear concealing clothing to avoid being noticed

Memory.value: When I have memories of what happened I sometimes hear things in my head that I heard during the frightening event.
Something in my surroundings can instantly bring back the full memory without warning
My memories of the event come in disconnected pieces that do not fit together

Negative Appraisals.value: I was betrayed by someone I trusted
The event happened to me because of the sort of person I am
My beliefs about how the world works have been completely destroyed

vignette: Amir's eyes would often dart towards the windows of his community center office, scanning the rooftops for helicopters. The sound of their rotors was unmistakable, and it never failed to transport him back to that fateful night three years ago when his wife, Fatima, had attacked him in their home. He remembered the darkness, the feeling of being trapped, and the sound of sirens in the distance - or were they helicopters? The memories came in fragmented pieces, disconnected and jarring, like a puzzle he couldn't quite assemble. As Amir recounted that night to himself, he couldn't shake off the sense of betrayal. Fatima had been his rock, his partner in every sense of the word. How could she have turned on him like that? The thought still felt like a punch to the gut. He was certain that he must have done something to deserve it - that somehow, this was all his fault. This self-blame seeped into his daily life, making him question his own character and judgment. The memories would often ambush Amir without warning, triggered by the most mundane things: a dark alleyway, a particular smell, or even just the sound of Fatima's name being mentioned in conversation. When this happened, he'd feel like he was reliving that night all over again - the fear, the helplessness, and the overwhelming sense of chaos. It was as if his mind had created a feedback loop, where each recollection reinforced the next, making it harder to escape. To cope with these episodes, Amir developed strategies to avoid being caught off guard. He started wearing baggy clothing to conceal himself in public, hoping to blend into the crowd and avoid drawing attention. He'd also become hypervigilant around people, constantly scanning for potential threats or signs of danger. This state of heightened alertness left him exhausted but also served as a reminder that he was still in control - or so he thought. As time went on, Amir found himself avoiding certain locations, especially those that reminded him of the night of the attack. He'd steer clear of dark spaces and try to stay in well-lit areas, even if it meant taking longer routes home from work. These habits had become second nature, but they also made him realize just how much his life was still being dictated by that one event. The more Amir dwelled on these memories, the more he felt like his world was shattered. His trust in others had been broken, and with it, his sense of security. He began to wonder if anything was truly safe or reliable. This constant questioning eroded his confidence, making him feel like a stranger in his own skin. One consequence of Amir's avoidance behaviors was the strain on his relationships with friends and family. They'd invite him to gatherings or events, but he'd decline, citing work commitments or fatigue. In reality, he just couldn't bear the thought of being in crowded spaces or confronting potential triggers. His wife had left him shortly after the incident, and now Amir felt like he was losing touch with everyone else too. As the months went by, Amir's inner world continued to darken. The memories still lingered, refusing to be silenced. He'd try to distract himself with work, but even his community organizing efforts seemed hollow without a sense of purpose or connection to others. It was then that he realized he needed help - not just to manage his symptoms but to rebuild his shattered life and find a way out of this suffocating cycle. Amir's voice trembled as he made the appointment with a therapist, unsure of what lay ahead but desperate for change. As he hung up the phone, he caught himself glancing towards the window once more, half-expecting to see helicopters hovering outside. The sound was just a memory now, but it still held the power to transport him back to that fateful night - and the darkness that had consumed his world ever since.
